title: Energy in Chemical Reactions
seo_title: Grade 7 Exothermic and Endothermic Worksheets: Hand Warmers and Cold Packs
standard_text: Undertake a design project to construct, test, and modify a device that either releases or absorbs thermal energy by chemical processes.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on energy in chemical reactions (NGSS MS-PS1-6): exothermic and endothermic processes, temperature data, and designing hand warmers and cold packs. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Some reactions release heat; others absorb it.
key_sub: Exothermic processes warm the surroundings (hand warmers). Endothermic processes cool them (cold packs).
body_html:
How to think about it

Chemical processes can release or absorb thermal energy.

  • Exothermic: releases energy, so the surroundings get warmer (hand warmers, burning, calcium chloride dissolving).
  • Endothermic: absorbs energy, so the surroundings get colder (instant cold packs, baking soda and vinegar).

Engineers use these processes to design warmers and cold packs. They test with a thermometer, compare against criteria (how hot or cold, how long) and constraints (cost, safety, size), and modify one thing at a time, such as the amount of a substance.

Example

Water goes from 21 °C to 9 °C after a powder is added. Exothermic or endothermic?

It got colder.

Energy was absorbed.

Answer: endothermic

Example

Which process would you use for a hand warmer?

You need heat released.

Answer: an exothermic one

Common mistakes

  • Saying a cold pack releases cold. It absorbs heat.
  • Mixing up exo (out) and endo (in).
  • Changing several things at once when improving a design.

faq.q: What is the difference between exothermic and endothermic?
faq.a: Exothermic processes release thermal energy and warm the surroundings. Endothermic processes absorb thermal energy and cool the surroundings.

faq.q: How does an instant cold pack work?
faq.a: When the inner pouch breaks, a substance dissolves in water and absorbs thermal energy, so the pack feels cold.

faq.q: How do you improve a hand-warmer design?
faq.a: Test it, compare the results with the criteria and constraints, change one thing such as the amount of iron powder, and test again.

items.e: The surroundings get warmer, so energy is released.

items.q: Why does a cold pack feel cold?

items.e: Cold is the absence of heat; energy moves into the pack.

items.q: What is an endothermic process?
c: one that absorbs thermal energy, so the surroundings get colder
items.e: Endo = in. Energy goes in.

items.q: Omar observes that steel wool burns in a flame. Is this reaction exothermic or endothermic?

items.q: In a design project for a cold pack, which is a constraint?

It must cost less than $2 to make.
It must feel cold on skin.

items.q: Which tool is most important for testing a hand-warmer design?

items.q: Why do hand warmers stay sealed until you open them?
c: They need water from the ground.

items.e: Iron reacts with oxygen and releases heat.

items.q: Photosynthesis takes in energy from sunlight. What kind of process is it?
